annotation_description: Played Overgrown Tomb on turn 1 instead of Blooming Marsh. Blooming Marsh enters untapped for free when you control 2 or fewer other lands (perfect for turns 1-3), while Overgrown Tomb costs 2 life to enter untapped. Playing Blooming Marsh first preserves the option to play Overgrown Tomb untapped later when Blooming Marsh would enter tapped (turn 4+).

Playing Breeding Pool on turn 1 requires paying 2 life to have it enter untapped for casting Llanowar Elves. Hushwood Verge enters untapped for free and can tap for {G} unconditionally (its {W} ability requires a Forest/Plains, but {G} is always available). Playing Hushwood Verge first would save 2 life while still enabling Llanowar Elves, and the Breeding Pools can be played on later turns when the life payment may matter less or they can enter tapped.

Haiku Coach missed their land drop for turn 2. They only have one land (Overgrown Tomb) on the battlefield and have multiple lands in hand. The board state shows only one land, meaning they haven't played a land this turn yet. Playing Blooming Marsh (which would enter untapped since they control two or fewer other lands) would allow them to cast Town Greeter this turn with the two mana available, helping develop their board and mill toward their game plan. Missing a land drop on turn 2 is a significant tempo loss.

Missed their Turn 2 land drop entirely. The game offered 4 land options to play, but the player incorrectly believed they had already used their land drop. With only 1 land (Overgrown Tomb) on the battlefield on Turn 2, this sets them a full turn behind on mana development while trying to reach 8 mana for Bringer of the Last Gift.

Failed to cast Spider Manifestation when there was sufficient mana available. Two untapped Breeding Pools provide 2 mana, exactly enough for Spider Manifestation's {1}{R/G} cost. Additionally, should have played Hushwood Verge as a land drop first for even more available mana. Spider Manifestation as a mana dork would significantly accelerate toward Craterhoof Behemoth.

Playing Multiversal Passage instead of Hushwood Verge costs 2 life unnecessarily (or enters tapped). Hushwood Verge enters untapped for free since they control Forests (Breeding Pool), and provides {G} which is what they need for Craterhoof Behemoth. Multiversal Passage should be saved for a later turn when a specific basic land type is needed that Hushwood Verge can't provide.

Breeding Pool provides U/G mana, but Haiku Coach has no blue cards in hand. Blooming Marsh would enter untapped for free (3rd land, 2 or fewer other lands) and provide B/G, which is more relevant for Bitter Triumph (1B), Formidable Speaker (2G), and Bringer of the Last Gift (6BB). Playing Breeding Pool either costs 2 life to enter untapped or enters tapped, and provides unnecessary blue mana.

Cast Bitter Triumph before playing a land drop. With Blooming Marsh or Watery Grave in hand, the land should be played first to preserve maximum mana options. Additionally, Formidable Speaker could have been considered first since it also involves a discard and provides a tutor effect, which could inform what to discard to Bitter Triumph.

Targeted Spider Manifestation (a vanilla 2/2) with Bitter Triumph instead of Gene Pollinator, which likely has more impactful abilities for generating ongoing value through token creation/copying. The 2/2 body is the least strategically important target compared to a creature with repeatable abilities.

Only attacked with one Mockingbird 1/1 flyer when both could attack freely. The opponent has no untapped blockers and no flying creatures, so both Mockingbirds could deal damage with zero risk. This leaves 1 free damage on the table.

Chose to tutor for Deceit when Overlord of the Balemurk was available. Overlord can be cast for impending cost {1}{B} very cheaply, mills cards to fill the graveyard, and synergizes strongly with the Bringer of the Last Gift already in hand. Deceit requires 6 mana to hardcast or evoke for a one-shot bounce/discard, which is less impactful given the opponent's wide board.

Attacking all creatures including mana dorks (Llanowar Elves, Gene Pollinator) into a 2/4 Formidable Speaker that can block and kill one. The Mockingbirds have flying and can't be blocked by the Speaker anyway. Risking a mana producer for at most 1 extra damage when Craterhoof Behemoth (8 mana) is in hand and needs mana acceleration.

Evoking Deceit for {U/B}{U/B} by paying {U}{B} (one blue from Breeding Pool, one black from Blooming Marsh/Overgrown Tomb) means neither the {U}{U} nor {B}{B} condition is met, so no ETB ability triggers. The creature enters and is immediately sacrificed for zero value, wasting a card from hand.

Copying Town Greeter (1/1) instead of Formidable Speaker (2/4) with a Craterhoof Behemoth in hand. Formidable Speaker provides a larger body for Craterhoof's buff, has an untap ability that could help reach 8 mana for Craterhoof, and the ETB tutor could optionally find another creature. Town Greeter's mill-for-land is speculative.

The player has two Mockingbirds (both 1/1 flyers) and Haiku Coach has no flyers to block. Both can attack freely for 2 damage total against 13 life. The player only selected one Mockingbird to attack instead of both. While neither attack is lethal, there's no reason not to attack with both since they can't be blocked and the opponent is at 13 life. Every point of damage matters, especially when the player is at only 9 life and needs to close the game quickly.

chosen_display: Formidable Speaker — {1}, {T}: Untap another target permanent. [Activate]
annotation_description: Evoking Deceit for {U/B}{U/B} by paying U+B means neither the {U}{U} nor {B}{B} ETB condition is met, so the creature enters with no effect and is immediately sacrificed. This wastes a Deceit card for absolutely nothing.

Attacking with Multiversal Passage (an earthbended land turned 1/1 creature) into an untapped Overlord of the Balemurk 5/5 risks losing a valuable mana source. The opponent can block any attacker and will likely block the most valuable one. Losing Multiversal Passage means losing a land/mana source needed to eventually cast Craterhoof Behemoth ({5}{G}{G}{G}). The marginal 1 damage from sending the land creature in (3 damage instead of 2 getting through) is not worth the risk.
